items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: Matches the task brief exactly: chose fix (b), corrected the ITERATE_RETENTION comment + module docstring bullet + F5c.md's retention section to state the cap is approximately 50 (pins add on top; cross-worktree merges can overshoot by one per branch, self-heals next append), added a regression test. No extra features beyond the brief; FR-/ADR-collision family left untouched as explicitly out of scope.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: No runtime logic changed -- comments/docs only plus a new test. No new error paths introduced.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input, no secrets, no auth/permission surface touched.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: New tests assert outcomes (file counts, surviving run_ids) not implementation internals. test_two_independent_worktrees_merge_one_over_cap proves the reproduction (cap+1); test_next_append_on_the_merged_tree_self_heals_to_cap proves the fix's central claim (self-heal back to cap). Deterministic seeding, no flakiness. Ran green: 12/12 in the retention test group, 699/699 in the wider shared suite.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New test file follows the sibling test_retention_race.py's helper/fixture conventions (confirmed by code-reviewer across two passes); shared/scripts/tools/append_iterate_entry.py stays at exactly its pre-existing anti-ratchet baseline (436 lines) -- no bloat-gate exception needed.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: No serialized format's producer or consumer behavior changed -- this is a documentation/comment correction plus a test proving pre-existing (unchanged) retention behavior. touches_io_boundary did not fire (confirmed via risk_detectors.is_io_boundary_change over the changed file list).
